title: What People Would Give up to Live Longer — Survey
paragraphs: Would you really give up something you love if it meant you could live longer? A new survey in the US asked people this question.
The survey was done for National Geographic magazine. In 2026, it asked 1,000 adults in the US about their thoughts on aging and living longer.

The results showed that most people care more about living healthily than living for a long time. About 64% said they would accept a shorter life if they could be sure that they would stay healthy in body and mind until the end.

People were also asked what they would give up for 10 more years of healthy life. About one in three said they would stop drinking alcohol forever. More than 20% said they would give up social media, sugar or coffee and other drinks with caffeine. About 18% said they would stop traveling by plane, and 13% said they would give up their car or their job. Only 15% said they would give up their favorite food. However, almost 20% said they would not give up anything at all.
Money is also a worry for many people. About 63% said they were worried that their money would run out if they lived too long.

Many people also had concerns about new medical treatments that try to slow aging. About 72% were worried about the risks. About two-thirds also worried that only very rich people would be able to pay for these treatments.
Interestingly, 61% said they would stop their body from getting older at a certain age if they could.
